description: Multimode filter and resonator with low pass, band pass, high pass and a sweepable notch, which self-oscillates as a sine wave

params.text: Sets the cutoff of the low pass and high pass and the centre frequency of the band pass and notch, roughly 16Hz to 16KHz
In the down position a fixed level tanh circuit soft clips the input signal; in the up position that limiting is bypassed
Sets the level of the signal at the input, silent at the bottom and full amplitude at the top; with limiting engaged the centre is the general purpose working point
Tunes that frequency finely around the setting of the COARSE knob
In the up position the band pass output feeds back into the input, so raising Q brings the filter to self-oscillation
Sets the depth of exponential frequency modulation from the FM input, inverting the voltage anticlockwise of centre
Sets the resonance, the amount of feedback from the filter's output to its input
Offsets the notch frequency from the centre frequency, marked in multipliers from a quarter to four times, and changes the notch output alone

inputs.text: The audio input, which reaches all four filter outputs at once
An audio input that is inverted before the filter, and whose level falls as Q rises
A rising edge pings the resonance, without moving the cutoff frequency
Shifts the cutoff at a volt per octave, and tracks pitch when the filter self-oscillates
Exponential frequency modulation of the cutoff, scaled by the FM attenuverter
Shifts the resonance, -8V to 8V summed with the Q knob
Shifts the notch offset, 0-5V summed with the NOTCH knob, and changes the notch output alone

outputs.text: Low pass output, with harmonics above the cutoff attenuated
Band pass output, with harmonics above and below the centre frequency attenuated
High pass output, with harmonics below the cutoff attenuated
Notch output, with harmonics in the stop band attenuated; at the extremes of the NOTCH knob it becomes a copy of the low pass or the high pass

inputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
